routes.label: Use the place value of the repeated block

question: A six-place number is formed by repeating a three-place number; for example, \(256{,}256,\) or \(678{,}678,\) etc. Any number of this form is always exactly divisible by:
solution:
Let \(k\) be the three-digit number, so \(100\le k\le999\). In the six-digit number, the first copy of \(k\) has been shifted three places to the left, multiplying its value by \(1000\). The second copy contributes another \(k\). Thus the number is
\[
1000k+k=1001k.
\]
Its quotient upon division by \(1001\) is exactly the integer \(k\), so divisibility by \(1001\) always holds. Also, \(1001=7\cdot11\cdot13\), so all three smaller divisors occur together, rather than any one of them only. The answer is \(1001\), choice E.
